ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a complementary push-pull power amplifier circuit; the output node on the right is connected to the upper end of the load resistor R_L, and the lower end of R_L is grounded; the load voltage u_o is marked as positive at the upper end and negative at the lower end. The figure also marks VT_1, VT_2, VD_1, VD_2, and the positive and negative power supply terminals ±V_CC. Then reason: the problem gives R_L = 8 Ω, and the voltage across the load U_o = 6 V. The output power is the power consumed on the load resistor, so P_o = U_o^2 / R_L = 6^2 / 8 = 36 / 8 = 4.5 W. When U_o has already been given, V_CC and the information about ignoring the transistor saturation voltage drop do not affect this calculation.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it is a complementary push-pull amplifier with the output node driving the resistor R_L to ground, and u_o marked with + at the top of R_L and − at ground. From the text take R_L = 8 Ω and U_o = 6 V. Since output power is the power dissipated in R_L and U_o is the load voltage, compute P_o = U_o^2/R_L = 6^2/8 = 4.5 W. The supply voltage and ignored saturation drops are not needed once U_o is given.
